history.summary: Shri Laxmi Narsimha Temple at Nira Narsingpur (NOT Pune city) is an ancient Vaishnavite temple at the confluence of the Bhima and Nira rivers at the southeastern tip of Pune district. Worship follows the Madhva sampradaya under Uttaradi Math, with Deshastha Madhva Brahmins as priests and rituals per Madhvacharya's Tantra Sara Sangraha. The present Peshwa-style temple on a small hillock (33 steps to the west entrance) was rebuilt by Raghunath Rao Vinchurkar in 1787. It is the kuldaiwat (family deity) of many Marathi families and was revered by the Vijayanagara rulers; Samarth Ramdas worshipped here twice en route to Pandharpur. Tirtha Yatra notes two sacred rivers and greenery around the site; the spot is popularly called Dakshin Prayag.

name: Laxmi Narasimha Temple
town: Nira Narsingpur (Indapur taluka; CSV town 'Pune' means Pune district, not the city)
town_description: Nira Narsingpur is a village in Indapur taluka, the last village of Pune district on its southeastern edge, at the common point of Indapur (Pune) and Madha/Malshiras talukas (Solapur). It sits at the confluence of the Bhima and Nira rivers, behind the Laxmi Narsimha temple. An agrarian village on the Pune-Solapur corridor, it draws steady pilgrim traffic as a Narasimha kshetra and is described by devotees as Dakshin Prayag.

travel.road: On the Pune-Solapur highway (NH-65) corridor via Indapur, about 110 km southeast of Pune city (verify).
